title: Scheduled Task Persistence
description: Windows Scheduled Tasks can be created or modified to execute attacker-controlled code at logon, on a schedule, or on specified events, providing a durable persistence mechanism. Weak permissions on task definitions or on the programs they invoke can also enable privilege escalation.
businessImpact: Moderate --- scheduled tasks give an attacker reliable persistence and, when running as a privileged account, a route to code execution with elevated rights.
remediation:
- Baseline and monitor scheduled tasks; alert on creation or modification of tasks.
- Restrict permissions on task definitions and the executables/scripts they run.
- Enforce least privilege for accounts used to run tasks.
- Investigate unexpected tasks as potential indicators of compromise.
